problem: Suppose that $f(x,y)=-7xy.$ Which of the following shaded areas gives the solution to the inequality $f(x,y)\le 0?$

examples.knowledge_point: Identifying Quadrants Where a Function Is Positive or Negative
examples.problem: Suppose that $f(x,y) = -6x^2y.$ Determine the region that gives the solution to the inequality $f(x,y) \geq 0?$
examples.worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=0$ and $y=0.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below. Since we have an "or equal to" inequality, we use solid lines to divide the plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14004890/assets/c35c98904d2a0d0d6d49c582cd9f9dba9d96e91ae0da5deb2d329f38f77532e3.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14004890/assets/9340582eaad37c4ce1e0c8cbcdce48faec1e36c3c05adbedd61aa2de7168fd2f.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $-6x^2$ | $y$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-Left | $(-1,1)$ | $\color{red}-$ | $\color{blue}+$ | $\color{red}-$ |
| Top-Right | $(1,1)$ | $\color{red}-$ | $\color{blue}+$ | $\color{red}-$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(-1,-1)$ | $\color{red}-$ | $\color{red}-$ | $\color{blue}+$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(1,-1)$ | $\color{red}-$ | $\color{red}-$ | $\color{blue}+$ |

 

Finally, on our diagram, we shade in the solutions to $f(x,y) \geq 0$ using the *last* column of the table above.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14004890/assets/17dd9e10234b6a69123241a882e267d95d505d1944d7c31ef563f9ac06b990af.png)

feedback.problem:
Consider the expression $f(x,y)=6{x}^{3}y.$ What are the missing entries in the following sign table of $f(x,y)?$

| $y>0$ |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<0$ |  |  |
|  | $x<0$ | $x>0$ |
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=0$ and $y=0.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14004890/assets/c35c98904d2a0d0d6d49c582cd9f9dba9d96e91ae0da5deb2d329f38f77532e3.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14004890/assets/9340582eaad37c4ce1e0c8cbcdce48faec1e36c3c05adbedd61aa2de7168fd2f.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $6{x}^{3}$ | $y$ | $f(x,y)$ |

| Top-Left | $(-1,1)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Top-Right | $(1,1)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |

Using the *last* column of the table above, we get the following picture:

| $y>0$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
